description: we’re relentless rookies, engineering students from jnn college of engineering, shivamogga, building a health monitoring system for astronauts. we love electronics, embedded systems and wearable sensors, with hands-on work on raspberry pi, esp32 and biosignals like heart rate and oxygen levels. join us if you want to build real tech that could save lives in space. we’re looking for people skilled in machine learning, data analysis, app or web development and user interface design.
summary: On long missions, astronauts must spot health changes in themselves. At Mars, a message to a doctor on Earth takes 3 to 22 minutes each way. VitalOrbit is an offline-first self-health monitor that turns a 3-minute daily check-in into a clear, colour-coded health picture and tells the astronaut exactly what to do next. Heart rate can come from a fingertip on the phone camera (photoplethysmography), a Bluetooth chest strap, an Apple Health export, or voice entry, and a reaction-time test measures fatigue. Beyond textbook ranges, VitalOrbit compares each astronaut with their own baseline and forecasts problems days ahead. An interactive body map links every reading to NASA's named spaceflight health risks (15 of 17 covered). Gamified routines keep countermeasures on track, and one tap sends a structured report to a Mission Control console that simulates the real light-time delay. It adapts to the space station, a lunar base or rover, a Mars transit or a Mars base.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

VitalOrbit is a self-health monitor for astronauts on long missions. It gathers 10 health indicators (heart rate, blood pressure, fasting blood glucose, body temperature, blood oxygen saturation, sleep, mood, exercise, water intake and radiation dose) plus symptoms and a reaction-time fatigue test. Every reading is rated Nominal, Watch or Act / report, with a plain-language explanation and the next steps to take.

Screens: Dashboard (health score, smart insights, indicator tiles, "what to do today", 5-hazard exposure) · Daily check-in (live status while typing, how-to-measure guides, voice entry) · Vitals scan (camera, Bluetooth strap, Apple Health import) · Fatigue test · Body map (9 body systems tagged with NASA risk names) · Trends & forecast · Routine & rewards · Learn · Report to Earth (text, PDF, CSV) · Mission Control (crew health matrix and delayed communications) · NASA data & coverage.

Live app: https://mevikaskulkarni.github.io/vitalorbit/

HOW IT WORKS

1. Reference-range rules plus context rules: a 3-day low-mood streak, a 7-day exercise load, a radiation budget against NASA's 600 millisievert career limit, and a headache + blurred-vision combination that flags Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome.

2. Personal-baseline anomaly detection: a z-score against the astronaut's previous 14 days ("unusual for you").

3. Least-squares linear regression over the last 10 days forecasts when a reading will cross a limit.

4. Camera photoplethysmography: red-channel averaging, moving-average detrending, peak detection, median beat interval and a rhythm-consistency quality score.

5. Standard Bluetooth Heart Rate Service, Apple Health export import, and speech recognition with a number parser.

6. A psychomotor vigilance test with lapses and false starts, compared with the astronaut's own history.

7. Mission settings (space station, lunar base or rover, Mars transit, Mars base) change gravity, radiation baseline, exercise target and signal delay; long delays tell the crew to act onboard first.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Astronauts can assess themselves without real-time ground support, catch slow trends early, measure quickly and consistently, and keep up countermeasure habits. Flight surgeons receive structured summaries instead of raw data. On Earth, the same approach can help remote and elderly patients.

TOOLS

React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Zustand, jsPDF, Web Bluetooth, Web Speech API, camera access (getUserMedia), Service Worker. Hosted on GitHub Pages; works offline as a Progressive Web App.

DEMO DATA AND LIMITS

The app opens with 28 days of simulated data for three fictional crew members. It is a prototype with illustrative thresholds, not a medical device.

SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) USE

Developed with Claude (Anthropic): it generated and debugged most of the code, suggested feature ideas that the team reviewed, helped draft documentation, and wrote the script that recorded the demo video (watermarked). Also stated in the README and source code.
dataRefs: NASA Human Research Program — 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight (hazard exposure panel and hazard-driven features)
NASA Human Research Program — Risks of Human Spaceflight (coverage of all 17 named risks; risk tags on the body map)
NASA Human Research Program — Ongoing HRP Research (Standard Measures, ARCHeR, Tempus Pro, Thigh Cuff, Zero T2, Immune Biomarkers shaped our indicators)
projectRefs: Canadian Space Agency — Monitoring radiation for astronaut health (neutron share of station dose; dosimeter-feed design)
Canadian Space Agency — Why do we conduct science experiments in space? (deep-space risk factors became our four mission environments)
Claude by Anthropic — Super Intelligence (SI) tool used for code, documentation, feature ideas and the demo recording
Open-source libraries: React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Zustand, jsPDF, lucide-react icons (full list in package.json)
